notes: Small, cheap fallback for tight-VRAM machines. Weaker reasoning than newer 7-8B models — benchmark it, don't assume it wins its tier.
Older but consistently light on refusals. Good baseline to compare newer models against.
13B step up if a PC has the VRAM for it.
Cognitive Computations' Dolphin fine-tune of Llama 3 — explicitly tuned to be compliant/uncensored while keeping Llama 3's reasoning. Strong default pick for 8GB-class cards.
Newer Dolphin generation (Llama 3.1 base). Benchmark against dolphin-llama3:8b — whichever wins on this hardware becomes the 8GB-tier default.
Lighter guardrails than base Llama/Mistral instruct models, strong general capability. Worth having in the mix even if it's not the least-refusal option — capability matters too.
Mixtral MoE — only ~13B active params per token so it's faster than the param count suggests, but full weights still have to fit in VRAM. 24GB cards will likely need a lower quant (see notes below).
Dolphin fine-tune of Mixtral — the strongest low-refusal option in this list if the hardware has 24GB+ VRAM. Same VRAM caveat as nous-hermes2-mixtral.
Only worth benchmarking on a 48GB+ card. Best reasoning in this list if the hardware supports it.
